status_html: Research preview · figures to 31 August 2026, updated 18 October 2026. Real figures and estimates from public sources, not yet reviewed by a person. Every number has a likely range and a source; gaps are filled with estimates, never left at zero. Method and data: GitHub. Corrections: Reddit or a GitHub issue.

trade.name: UN Comtrade, IMF trade statistics and Eurostat: goods trade with Russia and Ukraine
trade.note: own reports first, then partner (mirror) reports, IMF and estimates; 2026 is January to August

nonreport.name: Trade with Russia for partners that do not report (Cuba, Venezuela, Syria, Libya, Iran...): tanker tracking, official statements
nonreport.note: Russian supplies given on credit or as aid are Russian support, not money to Russia: only the paid share counts

kiel.name: Kiel Institute, Ukraine Support Tracker Release 31 (published 8 Oct 2026)

kiel_eu_share.name: EU-level aid split over member states by their contribution to the EU budget (Kiel method)

aid_gaps.name: Aid from countries outside the Kiel tracker: UN OCHA Financial Tracking Service and government reports
aid_gaps.note: countries with no record: 0, with a small upper bound based on what similar donors gave

refugees.name: Refugee hosting cost: national budget figures where reported, otherwise refugees hosted per year x cost per refugee calibrated on those budgets
refugees.note: Eurostat and UNHCR counts, US and Canadian programme arrivals; see research/2026-10/gaps/refugees-notes.md

energy.name: Energy switching cost, oil discounts and laundered oil: modelled per fuel from CREA, Eurostat, Comtrade and market prices

transit_gas.name: Russian gas by country of final use (Eurostat imports by origin, ENTSOG flows, CREA), passed on from transit countries
transit_gas.note: replaces the gas in customs data (UN Comtrade HS 2711, research/2026-10/gaps/customs_gas.json) and in the fossil fuel tracker; see energy2-notes.md; Austria, Switzerland and Hungary 2024 are estimates

laundered.name: Laundered oil: fuel made from Russian crude, assigned to the final buyer (trading hubs pass on what they resell), valued at the Russian crude inside it
laundered.note: hub resale shares are estimates; hub customers from UN Comtrade HS 2710 exports 2024; crude content 42-60% of the fuel value (CREA)

laundered_eu.name: Fuel made from Russian crude per EU member: Eurostat Comext HS 2710 imports by origin, refinery Russian-crude shares, CREA per-country checks
laundered_eu.note: final consumer after Dutch and Belgian resale; see research/2026-10/gaps/laundered_eu-notes.md

laundered_r6.name: Brunei's Hengyi refinery and Turkish ports relabelling Russian fuel: CREA, CSD, Eurostat Comext, UN Comtrade, Kpler-based reporting

refining.name: Russian crude refined in Turkey and India and exported as fuel: refinery reports, UN Comtrade, CREA, Global Witness
refining.note: the exported part is counted at the buyers as laundered oil; see research/2026-10/gaps/hub_buyers-notes.md

companies.name: KSE Institute and B4Ukraine: all taxes paid in Russia by foreign-owned companies, by home country
companies.note: reported for about 20 countries, allocated by company counts and investment for the rest; companies sold to Russian owners are not counted

company_taxes_r6.name: Company taxes in Russia: KSE checked against company reports (Raiffeisen, UniCredit, OTP, PepsiCo) and Bundesbank reinvested earnings

services.name: Services trade with Russia (tourism, transport, business services): Eurostat, OECD-WTO BaTiS, Bank of Russia

hidden.name: Gold and hidden payment channels to Russia not in customs data: Swissaid, Reuters, Hong Kong and Kyrgyz trade gaps

undisclosed.name: Undisclosed military aid beyond the Kiel tracker: Kiel policy briefs, national reports

private.name: Private donations to Ukraine: national donation totals (DZI, DEC, Candid) and a GDP-based model elsewhere

flowback_model.name: Own-industry share of military aid: modelled range from procurement evidence
flowback_model.note: no government except the US publishes this share

csis.name: CSIS, Where is the missing $100 billion in US aid for Ukraine

purl.name: Kiel Policy Brief 203 and Ukrainian government, NATO PURL purchases

flowback_default.name: Assumed own-industry share 20-70% (middle 40%) where no evidence was found

flowback_kiel.name: Own-industry share of military aid from Kiel's item-level coding (own stocks, domestic purchases, purchases abroad)
flowback_kiel.note: stocks refilled at home and items with no coded source are estimated per donor; see research/2026-10/gaps/flowback2-notes.md

eu_industry.name: EU-level military aid spent with each member's arms industry: Kiel item coding and SIPRI Top 100 production shares

other_mil.name: Military support to Russia: estimates from KIDA, INSS, Bloomberg and others
other_mil.note: rough indication, certainty D; mostly paid for by Russia

other_mil2.name: Military support to Russia: INSS, KIDA, Bloomberg, Ukrainian and Western intelligence, own valuation for Belarus
other_mil2.note: rough indication, certainty D; China left out because it overlaps trade data

military_rus_r6.name: Military support to Russia: Ukrainian and South Korean intelligence, Open Source Centre, the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, INSS, leaked Alabuga contracts, Russian procurement prices
military_rus_r6.note: market value of what Russia received; North Korea and Iran certainty C; see research/2026-10/gaps/military_rus_r6-notes.md

china_military.name: China's military support to Russia not in recorded trade: CSIS, RUSI, KSE, Reuters, US and EU findings
china_military.note: rough indication (D); recorded dual-use exports are already counted as sales to Russia; see research/2026-10/gaps/china_military-notes.md

people.name: Volunteers and recruited fighters: compiled estimates

shipping.name: Tanker shipping, insurance and ship sales serving Russian oil and LNG exports: CREA, KSE Institute, S&P Global, Windward, press reports
shipping.note: freight = barrels x freight rates, split by owner or manager country; see research/2026-10/gaps/shipping-notes.md

shadow_fleet.name: Tanker control by country: KSE Institute shadow-fleet tracker, Lloyd's List, S&P Global, Kpler and Windward reporting, US/UK/EU sanctions designations
shadow_fleet.note: beneficial owner or commercial controller, not the registered manager; see research/2026-10/gaps/shadow_fleet_r6-notes.md

reexports.name: Re-exports through trade hubs (UAE, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Turkey, Kyrgyzstan and others): UN Comtrade re-export flags and matched product trade
reexports.note: UAE and Georgia from their own re-export records; other hubs estimated per product chapter with hub shares; see research/2026-10/gaps/reexports-notes.md

residual.name: GDP gaps (UNSD, UN WPP, CEPAL), Russia's import gap by country of origin, Hong Kong gold composition

audit.name: Audit of 31 major countries against Kiel, CREA, Eurostat, national statistics and government reports

narrow.name: Official trade and services statistics and tourism counts for countries with wide ranges (Belstat, NBG, TÜİK, stat.uz, INSS)

audit2.name: Second audit: UAE gold and fuel, undisclosed aid, Russia's import-statistics gap, trend windows, border-priced imports

windfall.name: War-time price windfall on Russian fuel: payments minus the same volume at the prices a no-war market expected (pre-invasion forecasts and futures: IMF, World Bank, EIA, ECB, ICE)
windfall.note: fuel share of payments per year from own customs where measured (prices.json), else the pre-war import mix; fuel price indices (prices.json, energy2.json, gas_prices.json)

trend.name: Pre-war trade trends 2012-2021 in real terms (UN Comtrade, price indices), continued with a 3-year half-life

gas_prices.name: Russian gas prices per country: Eurostat Comext and UN Comtrade unit values, published contract prices, oil-formula estimates
gas_prices.note: see research/2026-10/gaps/gas_prices-notes.md; Turkey, Poland, Germany and Austria are modelled from neighbours or oil formulas

trend2.name: Pre-war trends for services (OECD-WTO BaTiS, Eurostat, Bank of Russia), foreign companies in Russia and Russian seaborne exports
trend2.note: travel fitted on 2012-2019 with the COVID rebound; see research/2026-10/gaps/trend2-notes.md

counterfactual.name: Expected trade without the war: models back-tested on 2008, 2013 and 2016 against holding 2021 flat (UN Comtrade, World Bank WDI and commodity prices, UN voting)
counterfactual.note: exports to Russia and trade with Ukraine follow a nowcast; imports from Russia and services keep 2021; see research/2026-10/gaps/counterfactual-notes.md

ua_trade_cf.name: Expected trade with Ukraine without the war: rolling back-tests on Ukraine's own history and on analogue partners (IMF WEO vintages, IMF DOTS)
ua_trade_cf.note: 2021 held flat for both flows; see research/2026-10/gaps/ua_trade_cf-notes.md

cf_bands.name: Ranges of the 2022-2026 total measured on the back-tests' cumulative errors; own bands for Mongolia, Yemen, Tajikistan and Moldova

weapons_value.name: Donated weapons at market value: GAO and DoD Inspector General (US drawdown valuation), UK National Audit Office, EU Peace Facility claims, used-equipment and munitions prices
weapons_value.note: factor = market value / recorded value per Kiel row; see research/2026-10/gaps/weapons_value-notes.md

state_finance.name: Rosatom projects abroad and Russia's state loans: World Bank International Debt Statistics (Russia as creditor), project and loan reporting
state_finance.note: drawdowns left out (they pay for work not counted); see research/2026-10/gaps/russia_state_finance-notes.md

company_flows.name: Company exits from Russia and Russian-owned companies abroad: Russian budget data, KSE and Yale exit lists, company reports, Bank of Russia balance of payments
company_flows.note: exit contribution and forced discount by home country; profits of Russian-owned firms by host country; see research/2026-10/gaps/company_flows-notes.md

refugees_net.name: Refugees' taxes and contributions: Czech Labour Ministry, Polish Ministry of Finance, Lithuanian ministry, OECD and IAB employment data; Poland's Aid Fund (BGK) spending
refugees_net.note: net = hosting cost - refugees' tax revenue; see research/2026-10/gaps/refugees_net-notes.md

ua_arms.name: Arms Ukraine bought abroad: Czech trade ministry licence reports, Czech ammunition initiative, Bulgarian defence exports, Kiel item coding, press investigations
ua_arms.note: only sales not already in customs trade or donors' own-industry flowback; see research/2026-10/gaps/ua_arms_purchases-notes.md

loans_value.name: Loans at economic value: Kiel loan terms (maturity, interest, grace), EU regulations, Ukraine's Eurobond yields; IMF, World Bank, EBRD and CEB lending by shareholding
loans_value.note: grant element at a 10% discount rate (6-15%); see research/2026-10/gaps/loans_value-notes.md

money_ledger.name: Where the money for Ukraine was spent: Kiel Ukraine Support Tracker item coding (release 31), CSIS, DSCA notifications, Ukraine's Ministry of Finance, replacement purchases (DoD Inspector General, NAO, government statements)
money_ledger.note: each euro assigned once to the economy where it was spent; see research/2026-10/gaps/money_ledger-notes.md

russian_arms.name: Russian arms exports by buyer: Rosoboronexport and FSVTS statements, SIPRI fact sheets, contract reporting (S-400, Su-35, Su-57)
russian_arms.note: change against expected payments, customs part removed; see research/2026-10/gaps/russian_arms_exports-notes.md

payment_agents.name: Payment agents settling Russia's trade: Bank of Russia balance of payments, Russian Finance Ministry and customs letters on agent commissions, press and sanctions reporting
payment_agents.note: fees kept by residents of the agent's country, against 2021; see research/2026-10/gaps/payment_channels-notes.md

frozen_reserves.name: Return denied on Russia's frozen central-bank reserves: Euroclear reports, Swiss SECO, EU Commission, G7 and central bank statements; rates per currency and year
frozen_reserves.note: per holding country; Euroclear and Clearstream shared with all EU members; see research/2026-10/gaps/frozen_assets-notes.md

value_kept.name: Value kept in the economy: OECD Trade in Value Added (TiVA, 2025 edition), defence-industry content studies; genuinely extra: production ramp-ups, trade-redirection studies
value_kept.note: value kept x genuinely extra, per country and kind of earning; see research/2026-10/gaps/value_kept-notes.md
